records.title: 1.6L EcoBoost Localized Cylinder-Head Overheating and Engine Fire (Recall 14V437)
records.description: Early 1.6L EcoBoost Fusions can suffer a localized lack of coolant circulation that overheats one corner of the cylinder head; the head cracks and pushes oil/coolant onto the hot exhaust, and vehicle fires occurred while driving or after shutdown. Ford recall 14V437 covers 2013 Fusion 1.6L vehicles built in a defined window; the failure mode is distinct from the 1.5L coolant-into-cylinder intrusion issue.
records.solution: Under recall dealers inspect for coolant-system leaks and reprogram the PCM and instrument cluster with an updated overheat-detection/limp-home strategy; damaged engines are repaired as needed. Owners should never keep driving after a coolant-loss/overheat warning. A cracked head from overheating typically requires head or long-block replacement out of warranty.
symptoms: Coolant loss with no obvious external leak
Engine overheating / temperature warning
White exhaust smoke or misfire
Smell of burning oil, smoke from engine bay
Fire while driving or after shutdown

records.title: 1.5L EcoBoost Coolant Intrusion into Cylinders - Internal Engine Block Failure
records.description: The 1.5L EcoBoost in 2014-2019 Ford Fusion is affected by the same open-deck cylinder block design defect as the Escape. Coolant leaks internally from the block passages into the combustion chambers due to insufficient sealing surface and porous block material that cannot maintain coolant pressure over time. Ford extended warranty coverage to 7 years/84,000 miles for short block replacement per TSB 19-2139 and TSB 19-2375. A consolidated class action lawsuit covers 2013-2019 Fusion and Escape with 1.5L, 1.6L, and 2.0L EcoBoost engines. Some owners have experienced engine failure with no warning - no check engine light before coolant hydrolocked the cylinder.
records.solution: Ford TSBs 19-2139 and 19-2375 cover short block and head gasket replacement under extended warranty (7 years/84,000 miles from warranty start date). Verify coverage at fordowner.com or call Ford Customer Relations 1-800-392-3673. Class action lawsuit for out-of-warranty reimbursement: lieffcabraser.com/defect/ford-coolant. Post-repair: Ford recommends monitoring coolant level and using only Motorcraft Orange coolant (VC-3-B).
symptoms: White or gray smoke from exhaust, especially on cold starts
Engine misfires with P0300-P0303 codes (1.5L is 3 cylinders in newer versions; earlier is 4-cyl)
Coolant level dropping without visible external leak
Sweet smell from exhaust
Coolant reservoir bubbling or pressurizing excessively
Engine overheating
Rough idle that clears up as engine warms
No warning light in some cases before engine fails

communityRecommendations.content: Ford's 7yr/84k extended warranty for the 1.5L EcoBoost short block is YOUR money - call 1-800-392-3673 and reference TSBs 19-2139/19-2375 before authorizing any repair. Do not let dealers deny coverage without escalating. FusionEnergiForum has documented hundreds of successful warranty claims.

Unlike most engine problems that show warning lights first, this failure can destroy your engine without a CEL. Some owners report zero warning signs before a hard start, white smoke, then engine death. Check coolant level monthly on any 2014-2019 Fusion 1.5L EcoBoost.

If your dealer claims they cannot replicate the problem or denies the extended warranty, escalate to Ford Customer Relations and request a "Technical Assistance Request." Reference TSB 19-2139. The FTC investigated Ford's concealment of this defect - dealers are obligated to honor the extended warranty.

records.title: 6F35 6-Speed Automatic Harsh/Delayed Shifting and Torque Converter Shudder
records.description: The 6F35 six-speed automatic is prone to harsh, banging, or delayed shifts (most often 2-3 and 3-4) plus a shudder/vibration when the torque converter clutch locks up at a steady 40-60 mph cruise. Root causes are worn valve-body separator-plate O-rings and bores that can no longer hold clean line pressure, clogged/worn shift solenoids, and torque-converter clutch degradation. Many units develop symptoms well before 100,000 miles. A 2019 class-action lawsuit accused Ford of concealing the 6F35 defect on Fusion and Escape.
records.solution: Start with a full fluid-and-filter service using the correct Mercon LV. For confirmed harsh shifts, reman or updated valve body with new solenoids is the durable fix; TCC shudder that survives a flush usually requires torque-converter replacement. Verify the transmission calibration is up to date (Ford released updated shift-strategy PCM/TCM reflashes). Severe internal wear = rebuild or reman transmission.
symptoms: Hard/banging upshifts especially 2nd-to-3rd
Shudder or vibration cruising at 40-60 mph
Delayed engagement into drive or reverse
Slipping or flaring between gears
Transmission overheating warning

records.title: AWD Power Transfer Unit (PTU) Overheating and Fluid Leak Failure
records.description: On AWD Fusions the Power Transfer Unit holds only about a quart of gear oil with no dipstick, service interval, or cooling, sitting next to hot exhaust and transaxle. The fluid cooks and breaks down, becoming thick, gummy, and black, and the seals leak. Owners report a burning smell in the cabin, whining/growling, and eventually PTU seizure that can damage the transmission. Failures often occur relatively early in the car's life.
records.solution: Preventive fluid changes roughly every 30,000 miles greatly extend PTU life even though Ford lists it as filled-for-life. A leaking unit may be resealed for $400-$600 if caught early; a failed PTU requires replacement, which dealers quote from ~$1,600 up to ~$3,100 including labor.
symptoms: Burning oil smell in cabin
Whining, growling, or grinding from center of vehicle
Brown/black fluid leak near transaxle/axle area
Vibration or shudder under acceleration
Loss of AWD function

records.title: Door Latch Pawl Spring Failure - Door Opens While Driving
records.description: The 2013-2016 Ford Fusion is subject to multiple door latch recalls due to the pawl spring tab inside the side door latches fracturing. The design is susceptible to failure in high-temperature and high-humidity climates. Over 90% of warranty claims occurred in hot/humid states. A fractured pawl spring tab causes the door to fail to latch properly, or to open unexpectedly while the vehicle is moving. Ford issued multiple recalls covering Fusion: the original 14S17, expanded with 16V643, and additional recalls covering 2014-2016 Fusion specifically. Ford and Lincoln recalled over 2 million vehicles total across multiple model lines for this defect.
records.solution: Ford Safety Recalls 14S17 / 16V643 / and subsequent recalls - dealers replace all affected side door latches at no charge. No mileage limit. Check safercar.gov or fordowner.com with VIN. The latches are replaced free regardless of current ownership. Multiple subsequent recalls covered additional years and models with the same issue.
symptoms: Door will not latch shut (bounces back when closed)
Door ajar warning chime or light with door apparently closed
Door opens while vehicle is moving
Wind noise from door area
Door latch mechanism feels loose or spongy

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 16V643 - Ford Fusion Door Latch Safety Recall
Ford and Lincoln Recall Over 2 Million Vehicles - Consumer Reports

communityRecommendations.content: Multiple recalls cover this issue - check safercar.gov with your VIN to see ALL applicable recalls for your specific Fusion. This is a safety defect. Door opening at speed increases ejection risk. Free dealer repair required.

If your door won't close before the recall is done: a temporary workaround is looping a strong zip tie through the latch striker to prevent door from opening while driving. This is emergency-use only - get to dealer ASAP for the proper fix.
Failure rate is highest in states with hot, humid climates (FL, TX, GA, AL). If you live in these states and have a 2013-2016 Fusion, prioritize this recall even if your doors currently close fine.

records.title: Electronic Throttle Body Failure - Limp Mode and Wrench Light
records.description: The electronic throttle body suffers internal contamination/wear of the motor contacts, causing intermittent electrical failure rather than simple dirt buildup. The result is a sudden loss of power (limp/failsafe mode) with the amber wrench (powertrain) warning light, rough idle, or stalling, sometimes in traffic. Ford acknowledged the problem with extended-warranty program 13N03 for 2010-2013 models and Customer Satisfaction Program 16B32 for certain 2015-2016 vehicles including Fusion.
records.solution: For the limp-mode failure the throttle body must be replaced (cleaning does not fix internal electronic wear), followed by a mandatory throttle-body relearn to prevent high idle and driveability faults. Check whether the vehicle qualified for 13N03 or 16B32 coverage history.
symptoms: Wrench/powertrain warning light
Sudden loss of power / limp mode
Rough or surging idle
Stalling

records.title: EVAP Purge Valve Stuck/Leaking - Check Engine Light and Rough Running
records.description: The under-hood evaporative-emissions purge valve on 2010-2011 Fusion/Milan (2.5L DOHC and 3.0L) built on or before 3/4/2011 can stick open or leak, unmetered vapor entering the intake. This lights the MIL and sets a cluster of EVAP and lean/fuel-trim codes, and can cause rough idle or hard starts. It is a documented Ford pattern failure with a related TSB covering the affected build range.
records.solution: Confirm the purge valve holds vacuum and clicks when energized; replace the stuck/leaking purge valve (inexpensive part). Verify no cracked EVAP hoses, a properly sealing gas cap, and an intact charcoal canister before clearing codes. Smoke-test the EVAP system if large-leak codes persist.
symptoms: Check engine light on

records.title: Front Brake Hose Rupture - Loss of Brake Fluid and Longer Stopping (Recall 23S12)
records.description: A design flaw in the front brake hoses lets them rupture over time, leaking brake fluid and increasing stopping distance. Ford recalled roughly 1.2-1.28 million Fusion and Lincoln MKZ sedans (recall 23S12) in 2023 after an NHTSA investigation. A ruptured hose causes a low brake-fluid warning, a change in pedal feel, and a real crash risk from degraded braking.
records.solution: Under recall 23S12 dealers replace both front brake hoses and, where equipped, modify the hose routing and ride-height sensor at no charge. Owners noticing a soft/low pedal or brake warning light should stop driving and have the hoses inspected immediately.

records.title: HVAC Blend Door Actuator Failure - Clicking/Knocking Behind Dash, No Heat or AC
records.description: The plastic gears inside the HVAC blend-door actuator strip out, so the door can no longer move to route air correctly. The classic symptom is a repeated clicking or knocking noise from behind the dash (often at startup or when changing temperature), along with air stuck on one temperature, wrong vent output, or one side blowing hot while the other blows cold. It is one of the most common Fusion comfort complaints across all generations.
records.solution: Replace the failed blend-door actuator (driver side of the HVAC housing, accessed by dropping the glove box). After replacement, perform the actuator calibration: reconnect the battery, turn ignition to On without starting, and let the system self-learn its range for at least a minute. Parts are inexpensive; labor rises sharply if a deeper actuator requires dash removal.
symptoms: Repeated clicking/knocking noise behind dashboard
No heat or no cold air from vents
Temperature stuck on hot or cold
Different temperature from left vs right vents
Air blows from wrong vents

records.title: Hybrid High-Voltage Battery Degradation and Failure
records.description: Ford Fusion Hybrid spans two generations with different high-voltage batteries — degradation patterns differ. 1st-gen 2010-2012 (NiMH, ~1.4 kWh): typical degradation appears at 100,000-150,000 miles with reduced EV-mode range and increased ICE intervention. Replacement runs $2,500-$4,000 at independent hybrid specialists. 2nd-gen 2013-2020 (Lithium-ion, ~1.4 kWh): better thermal management has led to longer life on average but cell imbalance issues appear at 150,000+ miles. 'Stop Safely Now' warnings often precede full failure. 2013-2020 Energi PHEV variants share the architecture but with larger 7.6 kWh batteries — separate degradation curve. Owners should check cell balance via OBD-II scanner with hybrid module support (Forscan recommended).
records.solution: Check warranty first - Ford covers 8yr/100k miles (10yr/150k in CA, CT, MA, ME, MD, NJ, NY, OR, PA, RI, VT, WA states). If out of warranty, aftermarket/remanufactured battery packs from GreenTecAuto ($1,550-2,950 installed) are significantly cheaper than dealer replacement ($4,000-7,000). Individual cell replacement at specialized hybrid shops ($800-2,000) is an option if only specific cells have failed. Battery reconditioning is a temporary fix that may restore 60-80% of capacity for $300-800.
symptoms: Reduced electric-only driving range
Decreased fuel economy (gradual decline)
"Check Hybrid System" warning on dashboard
Slower-than-normal acceleration or power loss
Battery charge indicator drops faster than normal
Unusual noise from battery compartment area
Vehicle fails to start (complete battery failure)
Hybrid system shuts down and runs on gasoline only

records.title: MyFord Touch / SYNC 2 (APIM) Freezing, Black Screen, and Rebooting
records.description: The MyFord Touch / SYNC 2 system (driven by the APIM module) is widely reported to freeze, go black, reboot repeatedly, lose Bluetooth pairing, and drop audio or backup-camera display. The Accessory Protocol Interface Module (APIM) has a known tendency to fail, and Ford extended warranty coverage on the module for affected owners. Beyond annoyance, a blank screen can disable the backup camera and climate controls.
records.solution: Try a soft reset (hold Seek-up + Power until the screen goes black) and a Master Reset, then update SYNC software via USB. Persistent freezing/rebooting usually traces to a failing APIM, which is replaced and reprogrammed (as-built) at a dealer; check for any remaining extended-warranty coverage. Many owners retrofit later software or a replacement APIM.
symptoms: Touchscreen freezes or goes black
System reboots repeatedly while driving
Bluetooth/phone pairing failures
Backup camera image missing
Audio cuts out or controls unresponsive

records.title: Parasitic Battery Drain - Dead Battery / No Start (BCM & Modules)
records.description: Many Fusion owners report the battery going dead overnight or over a weekend from a parasitic draw. Common culprits are a module that fails to sleep - Body Control Module (BCM), APIM/infotainment, or amplifier - as well as the PATS anti-theft transceiver circuit on earlier cars. A healthy vehicle should draw under ~50mA at rest; failed modules keep the network awake and flatten the battery.
records.solution: Measure key-off current draw with a multimeter, then pull fuses one at a time until the draw drops to isolate the offending circuit/module. Repair or replace the module that will not sleep (commonly BCM, audio/APIM, or amplifier); reflash where required. Confirm the battery and alternator test good before condemning a module.
symptoms: Battery dead after sitting overnight or a weekend
Frequent jump-starts required
Clicking / no-crank no-start
Electrical gremlins or flickering
Short battery life

records.title: Electric Power Steering (EPS) Failure - Sudden Loss of Assist
records.description: 2014-2018 Ford Fusions use a different EPS module revision than the 2011-2013 recall (NHTSA 15V340) — but owners still report sudden loss of power steering assist, particularly at higher mileage. Without recall coverage, repairs are owner-paid: rack replacement typically $1,200-$2,000. Symptoms mirror the recalled generation (heavy steering, intermittent warnings, eventual full assist loss). For 2013 specifically, the 15V340 recall applies if the vehicle is without the 3.5L engine.
records.solution: Check safercar.gov with VIN for Recall 15V340/15S18 and 19V632 eligibility - free dealer repair. Out-of-recall: EPS rack assembly replacement ($1,200-$2,800). If experiencing intermittent "Service Power Steering" warning: try restarting vehicle as temporary workaround (does not fix underlying issue). Avoid car washes with high-pressure undercarriage spray aimed at steering gear area (accelerates bolt corrosion on 2013-2015 models).
symptoms: "Service Power Steering" warning message on instrument cluster
Sudden heavy steering requiring much more effort, especially at low speeds
Steering wheel becomes very difficult to turn
"Hill Assist Not Available" and "Service AdvanceTrac" warnings accompanying EPS failure
Intermittent loss of power steering that returns after restart
Complete steering assist loss at any speed
Grinding or clicking from steering column during turns

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 15V340 / Ford Recall 15S18 - EPS Motor Sensor Fault (2011-2013)
NHTSA Recall 19V632 - EPS Motor Attachment Bolt Corrosion (2013-2015)
US Closes 7-Year Probe Into Ford Fusion Power Steering Failures

communityRecommendations.content: Check safercar.gov NOW for recalls 15V340 and 19V632 - both provide free EPS repair. Recall 19V632 specifically covers corrosion of EPS motor bolts that can cause the motor to DETACH from the steering gear - a catastrophic failure at any speed.

If "Service Power Steering" appears, immediately slow down safely - steering effort is now entirely manual. Turning will require 3-4x normal effort. Do not attempt U-turns or parking lot maneuvers without extra caution. This is a safety-critical failure.

The "temporary fix" of restarting the car when EPS fails is documented - this can reset the fault and restore power steering temporarily. But this is a band-aid: the underlying EPS hardware must be inspected and repaired. Do not rely on the restart trick permanently.

records.title: Power Window Regulator Failure and Window Bounce-Back
records.description: Gen-2 Fusions have a long-running window-module/regulator problem. A common 'bounce-back' fault makes the window roll up, hit the top, and immediately drop back down, and worn regulator gears/cables cause clicking, chattering, or grinding and can drop the glass inside the door. The driver-door switch and window-module re-initialization are frequently involved. Documented across 2013-2016 and beyond.
records.solution: Re-initialize (relearn) the auto up/down after battery or module work; if that fails, replace the affected window regulator (and motor) and, if the switch tests bad, the master window switch. Some cases require the window system re-initialization at a dealer.
symptoms: Window rolls up then bounces back down
Window stuck, will not go up or down
Clicking/chattering/grinding from door
Auto-up/one-touch stops working
Glass drops into door

records.title: Shifter Cable Bushing Detaches - Vehicle Rollaway Risk (Recall 18S20 / 22S43)
records.description: A plastic bushing that attaches the shift cable to the transmission can degrade and pop off, so the transmission may be in a different gear than the shift lever indicates. The driver can shift to Park, remove the key, and walk away while the transmission is actually not in Park, allowing the car to roll away. Ford issued recall 18S20 in 2018 (~504,000 vehicles) and later expanded it as 22V413/22S43 after the first repair proved inadequate, adding a protective cap.
records.solution: Under recall (18S20, then 22S43) dealers replace the under-hood shift-cable bushing and install a protective cap at no charge. Owners should always set the parking brake. Out of warranty, the bushing is an inexpensive part but reattaching/replacing it correctly with the cap is essential to prevent recurrence.
symptoms: Vehicle rolls after being placed in Park
Shift lever position does not match actual gear
Difficulty shifting or shifter feels disconnected
Cannot remove key or key removal does not correspond to Park

records.title: Electric Power Steering Rack Failure (Recall 15V340)
records.description: NHTSA recall 15V340 covers 2011-2013 Ford Fusion (and Lincoln MKZ) without the 3.5L engine. An intermittent electrical connection in the steering gear can cause sudden loss of electric power steering assist while driving. Owners notice heavier steering effort especially at low speeds, increasing crash risk. Dealers check the Power Steering Control Module (PSCM) for DTCs; if any loss-of-assist codes are stored, the steering gear is replaced free. Note: 2010 Fusions had the same parts but were excluded from the recall — feds closed the probe without expanding scope. 2010-owner symptoms are real but uncovered by recall.
records.solution: Check if your vehicle is covered under Ford recall (2011-2012 Fusion/MKZ power steering failure recall - free repair). For non-recall vehicles, the electric power steering rack must be replaced as a complete unit since the motor and control electronics are integrated. RepairPal estimates $1,958-3,362 installed. Remanufactured racks from PWR Steer or Cardone are available at $800-1,500, significantly cheaper than new OEM ($2,000+). Have the alignment performed after rack replacement.
symptoms: Power steering warning message on dashboard
Steering becomes heavy or requires extra force
Intermittent loss of power steering assist
Steering wheel off-center after loss of assist
Clunking or grinding from steering column area
Complete loss of power steering (requires significant force to turn)
Steering assist comes and goes unpredictably
Check engine light or power steering fault code stored

communityRecommendations.content: If your Fusion suddenly loses power steering assist, you can still steer the car but it requires significant effort. Pull over safely and do not drive at highway speeds without power assist. Complete loss of EPAS is a safety hazard, especially in emergency maneuvers.

Remanufactured electric steering racks from PWR Steer or Cardone are $800-1,500 vs $2,000+ for new OEM. Independent shops can install them for $400-600 labor. This can save $1,000+ over dealer pricing. Always get an alignment after rack replacement.

records.title: Water Intrusion into Trunk/Tire Well - Wet Carpet and Corroded Modules
records.description: Fusion owners frequently find water pooling in the trunk/spare-tire well and wet rear carpet. Sources include leaking taillight gaskets/plastic rivet pass-throughs, deteriorated trunk and rear-window seals, and split spot-welds in the channel under the rear glass. Standing water risks rust and corrosion of trunk-mounted electronics (on hybrids the high-voltage battery and electronics sit in this area), plus musty odor and mold.
records.solution: Water-test to locate the entry point, then reseal or replace the taillight gaskets/rivet grommets, trunk weatherstrip, and rear-window seal; seal split spot-welds with seam sealer. Clear any blocked trunk/quarter-panel drain holes and dry the carpet/insulation thoroughly to prevent corrosion and mold.
symptoms: Water in spare-tire well
Wet or musty rear carpet
Water dripping near taillights
Foggy/condensation in trunk
Rust or corroded connectors in trunk
